basic_info: 46-year-old male presenting with chronic abdominal pain, constipation, and occasional diarrhea for approximately two years.
present_illness: The patient is a 46-year-old male with chronic abdominal pain localized to the mid-abdomen, just below the belly button. The pain is described as nagging and intermittent, with fluctuating severity. It is noted to improve with bowel movements. He also experiences constipation and occasional diarrhea over the past two years. Certain foods, like pasta with creamy sauce, seem to trigger his diarrhea. He has not experienced weight loss, night sweats, or significant changes in bowel habits, though he notes a stable weight and could stand to lose about 25 pounds. He has had changes in his bowel habits over the past two years, with constipation being more common lately, and he usually goes three to four times a week, but it can be hard to pass stool. He does not eat pasta with creamy sauce very often, maybe once every couple of weeks, but when he does, he usually has a small portion, which still seems to trigger the diarrhea. Other than that, he eats pretty regular portions of healthy foods throughout the day.
past_history: No relevant past medical history, no prior surgeries, no known allergies. Family history is unremarkable for gastrointestinal disorders. No endoscopic evaluations (colonoscopy or upper endoscopy) have been performed to date. No stool tests, such as fecal calprotectin or occult blood tests, have been performed.
physical_exam: Vital signs: temperature 36.8°C, heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 bpm, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Abdominal examination: soft, non-tender, no palpable masses, normal bowel sounds. No rectal bleeding noted on digital examination.
aux_exam: Abdominal CT scan (recent): unremarkable findings. No fecal calprotectin or occult blood tests have been performed. No endoscopic evaluations (colonoscopy or upper endoscopy) have been performed. No abdominal ultrasound or MRI performed in the past.
